Task created: EXP-002: identifiability toy experiment (designs x basis size x mismatch)

F-001 Material identifiability in this toy spectral CT model is set by the rank of the Poisson-weighted count Jacobian, not by the estimator: one energy-integrating measurement gives rank 1 on every sampled ray (cannot separate 2+ materials), dual-kVp gives rank 2 (separates 2 materials, median condition number 195), and dual-kVp cannot separate 3 materials (rank 2 < 3). Four photon-counting bins separate 3 materials but with 2.70x the iodine CRLB noise of dual-kVp 2-material at equal total photons.

F-002 The forward model plus per-ray Poisson MLE is statistically well-calibrated: empirical Monte-Carlo standard deviation of estimated line integrals matches the Cramer-Rao bound within 11% for every identifiable cell at 1e6 photons (0.87-1.11 across water/iodine/calcium), with zero LM convergence failures. This validates the forward model, Jacobian and estimator as a consistent stack.

F-003 Fitting a 2-material basis to 3-material data produces bias that does NOT shrink with photon count (bias ratio 1e6/1e5 = 0.89 and 1.02 versus 0.32 expected for noise-driven error), at 7-15x the noise floor: basis misspecification is a systematic error that more dose cannot fix.

F-004 PARTIAL FALSIFICATION of pre-registered prediction (f): a nominal-spectrum estimator on mismatched-spectrum data is NOT detectably biased in every design. 7 of 12 cells passed. All four dual-kVp cells on the 2-material phantom failed (bias only 0.73-1.77x its noise floor), as did one 4-bin cell. Photon-counting designs showed clear mismatch bias (6-8x floor) while dual-kVp did not. Interpretation (preliminary, needs a dedicated experiment): at +-10% tilt and +-2% energy scale the dual-kVp mismatch bias is at or below the detection floor of 20 realisations, so (f) was under-powered rather than physically wrong; an alternative explanation is that 2-material dual-kVp genuinely absorbs smooth spectral error into the basis coefficients. These are NOT distinguished by this experiment.

F-005 SUPERSEDES F-004. Spectral mismatch always produces genuine bias; the apparent 'no bias' cells were a detection-power and scope artifact of the pre-registered criterion. Noise-free calculation (MLE on EXACT expected counts from perturbed spectra, zero Poisson noise, 20cm water + 0.2 g/cm2 iodine): every condition gives nonzero bias. Relative to the 20-realisation detection floor (CRLB/sqrt(20)) at 1e6 photons: dual-kVp iodine tilt +-10% = 0.93-1.05x (genuinely at the floor: UNDER-POWERED, not unbiased), dual-kVp iodine energy-scale +-2% = 4.0-4.2x (CLEARLY BIASED: the original F-004 wording was wrong for this case), dual-kVp WATER tilt = 3.8-4.1x (the iodine-only criterion hid a large water bias), 4-bin photon counting = 9-21x on the 2-material phantom. Two defects in the pre-registered criterion: it scored iodine only, and it required 3x the floor at BOTH dose levels so the noisier 1e5 level dominated the verdict.

F-006 SUPERSEDES F-002. Empirical Monte-Carlo std agrees with the Cramer-Rao bound to within 12.5% (median over rays; range 0.875-1.106) for the three identifiable cells at 1e6 photons, with a systematic pattern (P2 cells low 0.87-0.95, P3 k=3 cells high 1.05-1.11) rather than scatter about 1. The sampling spread of this check is ~3-4% (median of per-ray std estimates over 26-54 rays, 20 draws each), so the deviation is real, not check noise. This is a SELF-CONSISTENCY check of Jacobian + sampler + MLE under one shared model and table: a wrong attenuation table or spectrum would pass it equally. It is not validation of physical fidelity.

F-007 SUPERSEDES F-001. Identifiability separates into a structural part and an empirical part. STRUCTURAL (forced by matrix shape, not an experimental result): with n_meas measurements and k unknown materials, rank <= min(n_meas,k), so 1 energy-integrating measurement cannot separate 2+ materials and dual-kVp cannot separate 3. EMPIRICAL (the real content): among designs that ARE identifiable, conditioning differs substantially and is dose-independent - dual-kVp 2-material median condition number 195 (max 506), 4-bin photon counting 2-material 99, 4-bin 3-material 217. Rank verdicts are robust: smallest/largest singular-value ratios are 2e-3 to 1e-2, so any threshold from 1e-2 to 1e-10 gives identical ranks. Noise cost at equal total photons, SAME basis size (k=2, iodine CRLB): 4-bin 0.0019 vs dual-kVp 0.0047 g/cm2, i.e. photon counting is 2.5x BETTER. The previously quoted 2.70x 'worse' figure compared M4 k=3 against M2 k=2 and confounded design with basis size; it is the price of estimating a third material, not a penalty of photon counting.

F-008 AMENDS F-003 (scope). The dose-independent misspecification bias is an IODINE LINE-INTEGRAL statistic in g/cm2 (not g/cm3 density), measured on 27 rays of the 3-material phantom with a 2-material estimator. Both designs agree (bias ratio 1e6/1e5: M2 0.89, M4 1.02; 7.0x and 15.0x their noise floors). Dose-independence of misspecification bias is expected from theory, so this is a confirmation that the implementation behaves correctly, not a discovery.
D-003 D-G pre-registration and review standards

F-009 SUPERSEDES F-005 (2nd independent review). Spectral mismatch ALWAYS biases a nominal-spectrum estimator, and on the real ray subset every condition is DETECTABLE with an appropriate test - no cell is genuinely 'unbiased'. Noise-free MLE on exact expected counts, 48 P2 rays, 1e6 photons, floor = rms(CRLB)/sqrt(20): dual-kVp iodine tilt +-10% gives rms/floor 0.82-0.92 BUT signed-mean z = +4.6/-5.2 (detectable); dual-kVp iodine energy-scale +-2% rms/floor 3.8-3.9, z = +-22; dual-kVp WATER tilt rms/floor 4.0-4.3, z = +-24 (a large bias the iodine-only criterion hid entirely); 4-bin photon counting on P2 is 21-38x floor. All fits converged. The pre-registered 3x-observed-rms criterion is DEFECTIVE: it compares a noise-inflated rms against an unsubtracted floor and so cannot distinguish 'no bias' from 'bias below the rms detection limit'. A signed-mean-over-rays test is the correct statistic. Supersedes the earlier 'under-powered, not unbiased' framing, which conceded too much to the defective criterion.

F-010 SUPERSEDES F-007 (2nd independent review). Identifiability: STRUCTURAL part (rank <= min(n_meas,k), so 1 measurement cannot separate 2+ materials and dual-kVp cannot separate 3) is arithmetic, not evidence, and holds at any threshold. EMPIRICAL part, on the real ray subset at 1e6 photons: rank verdicts are robust for rank thresholds 1e-3 to 1e-10 (100% full rank) but NOT at 1e-2, where the full-rank fraction collapses to 0% for dual-kVp k=2 and 4-bin k=3 and 58% for 4-bin k=2, because smallest/largest singular-value ratios are only 0.0020-0.0123. (The superseded F-007 wrongly claimed robustness up to 1e-2, contradicting the ratios quoted in its own sentence.) Median condition numbers: dual-kVp k=2 195 (max 506), 4-bin k=2 99, 4-bin k=3 217. At EQUAL basis size k=2 and equal total unattenuated photons, 4-bin photon counting has median iodine CRLB 0.00151 vs dual-kVp 0.00376 g/cm^2 = 2.5x better by median (2.4x by rms aggregation; the ratio is ray-dependent). This compares an idealised energy-weighted 2-exposure design against an idealised 4-window 1-exposure design with NO detector response, charge sharing or pile-up, so it is an upper bound on the photon-counting advantage.

F-011 AMENDS F-009 (two numerical/scope corrections from the 2nd reviewer's verdict check, verified by Opus). (1) The 4-bin photon-counting bias on P2 is 27-43x the floor over all 8 (condition x material) cells, NOT the 21-38x stated in F-009. (2) The dual-kVp iodine TILT case is MARGINAL and must not be quoted as strongly detectable: per-ray bias is only 0.66-0.75 of the floor and the signed-mean z of about 5 arises only by pooling 48 rays. (3) All z values are noise-free hypothetical power computed against a noise-only null, i.e. the bias an infinite-data experiment would see relative to a 20-realisation floor - they are NOT observed test statistics from the Monte-Carlo run. F-009's central claim (mismatch always biases; the rms criterion is defective; dual-kVp water tilt bias is large and was hidden by iodine-only scoring) is unaffected.

D-005 D-I AAPM benchmark: noiseless exact recovery + simplex-constrained 3-material inversion

F-012 AAPM 3-material conditioning, computed from the official starting-kit spectra and mu tables (md5-verified kit, 10 sample cases): the spectrum-weighted effective attenuation matrix is [[0.26697,0.31321,3.01182],[0.21930,0.24788,1.64238]] 1/cm for (adipose,fibroglandular,calcification) at 50/80 kVp. Adipose and fibroglandular are spectrally near-degenerate: column cosine 0.999834, i.e. 1.04 degrees apart. The unconstrained 2x3 null direction is [-0.723,+0.691,-0.008], confirming F-010's prediction concretely: adipose can be traded against fibroglandular with essentially no measurement change. Appending the sum-to-one row makes the 3x3 system full rank (singular values 3.697, 1.176, 0.00290) but POORLY CONDITIONED at cond=1273. Therefore the partition constraint restores identifiability but error in the adipose/fibroglandular direction is amplified ~1000x; exact recovery in the noiseless challenge data is possible, while any model mismatch or interpolation error is magnified by that factor. Image-domain linear inversion is expected to be far worse than the published model-based winners (6.8e-7).

F-013 AAPM phantom maps are a TWO-REGIME partition, not a plain simplex (verified directly on the 10 kit sample cases, case 0): the three maps sum to exactly 0 in 35.1% of pixels (air background, no fourth material class), to 1 within 4e-8 in 59.6%, and lie strictly between 0 and 1 in only 5.2% (boundary/partial-volume pixels). Maxima: adipose 1.0, fibroglandular 1.0, calcification 0.566 (10-case sample). A classical estimator must therefore handle air explicitly - imposing sum-to-one globally would be wrong for 35% of pixels - and the 5.2% transition pixels are where a hard two-class assumption will fail. Arrays verified: phantoms/images (N,512,512) float32, transmission (N,256,1024) float32 in (0,1].

F-014 F-012's null space is now demonstrated OPERATIONALLY, not just algebraically (synthetic data, src/ctsynth/aapm/classical.py + tests/aapm/test_classical.py). Unconstrained per-pixel inversion of the 2x3 AAPM system genuinely fails (max per-pixel error > 0.05 in volume fraction) and its error vector is parallel to the SVD null direction to <1e-6 deg; that independently-computed null vector lies 0.024 deg from the published F-012 vector [-0.723,+0.691,-0.008]. Crucially the error is INVISIBLE to the data: |e @ mu^T| < 1e-12, i.e. the wrong answer reproduces the measurements exactly. Adding the sum-to-one row restores a unique solution (exact recovery to ~1e-10 in float64 on noiseless synthetic tissue pixels) but amplifies measurement perturbation: the derived worst-direction amplification sigma_max(B^-1[:,:2])*|d|/|x| = 181 for a typical 50/50 adipose/fibroglandular pixel, matched to rel 1e-4, which is 0.14x cond(B)=1273 (below cond because the appended sum row is exact and unperturbed).

F-015 REFINES F-013 (boundary pixels are the hard case, not merely a partial-volume nuisance). In the two-regime AAPM partition, pixels whose three fractions sum strictly between 0 and 1 (~5% of the image) are mis-modelled by a sum-to-one estimator: the unit-sum row CONTRADICTS the measurement there, and that contradiction is amplified by the ~1273 conditioning, so the resulting error is far LARGER than the sum deficit (1 - sum) itself. Simplex projection only clips the result and does not fix the model error. Consequence for the benchmark: boundary-band error must be reported separately (it is, in the evaluation record), and an air/tissue decision rule is a MODELLING CHOICE, not a fact recoverable from the data - the implementation uses AIR_CUTOFF_PER_CM = 0.1 (half the smallest tissue mu from F-012), which is untested on real AAPM data.
EXP-003 EXP-004 AAPM synthetic smoke benchmark: classical baselines vs no-training reference

F-016 On SYNTHETIC AAPM-schema data (EXP-003/RUN-0003, 17 val cases, 32x32, noiseless), an exact-on-tissue estimator is WORSE THAN PREDICTING NOTHING by the official aggregate metric. classical_sum_to_one recovers tissue pixels to RMSE 1.29e-6 (near machine precision, as theory predicts for noiseless data) yet scores s1 = 1.179, far worse than the no-training zero_prediction reference (s1 = 0.430), because the 5-9% boundary band carries RMSE 3.84 with individual values up to 11.5 volume fraction (grossly unphysical). Simplex projection clips those outliers and wins (s1 = 0.0508) WITHOUT improving the model: its tissue RMSE is the same 1.2e-6. CONSEQUENCE: a pooled RMSE over a two-regime phantom is dominated by the smallest, most mis-modelled population, so reporting s1 alone would rank a clipped estimator above an exact one for the wrong reason. Regime-separated reporting is mandatory for this benchmark. Caveat: synthetic data only; boundary-band fraction and geometry differ from real AAPM data.
